Mixed_Signals: The root route is Composites because the title, abstract and main performance target are CF/PPS composites, but the paper also reports standalone PAAs sizing-agent properties and sized CF processability items.
A Coating overlay is loaded because PAAs are explicitly described as a sizing layer/film on the CF surface.

Raw_Evidence_Span: PAAs with various molecular weights were synthesized by mixing PDA and BPDA with ratios outlined in Table 1.
After sizing with L-PAAs, M-PAAs, and H-PAAs, the carbon fibers were designated as L-CF, M-CF, and H-CF, respectively.

Process_Text.original: PDA and BPDA were mixed according to Table 1, excess TEA was introduced, the mixture was stirred at 0 °C for 18 h, 4-MPA was incorporated as a capping agent, solid content was maintained at 15 wt%, and an intentional heat treatment was performed in an oven at 320 °C for 2 h to mimic thermal imidization.
Process_Text.simplified: Synthesize PAAs in water with BPDA:PDA:4-MPA = 4:5:2, TEA, 0 °C for 18 h, 15 wt% solids; heat treat at 320 °C for 2 h to form L-PI mimic.

Structure_Text.original: FT-IR and 1H NMR confirmed that PAAs had been successfully synthesized and fully thermally imidized at 320 °C. Molecular weight has little influence on the chemical structure of PAAs.
Structure_Text.simplified: PAAs chemistry confirmed; imidized PI formed after 320 °C heat treatment.

Process_Text.original: CF fabric was subjected to a desizing process by refluxing in acetone at 70 °C for 12 h. Subsequent to this, the fabric was thoroughly rinsed with deionized water and was dried at 90 °C, yielding desized CF (DCF).
Process_Text.simplified: Desize CF fabric in acetone at 70 °C for 12 h, rinse with deionized water, dry at 90 °C.

Raw_Evidence_Span: After sizing with L-PAAs, M-PAAs, and H-PAAs, the carbon fibers were designated as L-CF, M-CF, and H-CF, respectively.
L-CF's surface could not be adequately covered by the sizing agent L-PAAs, leaving grooves and some filamentous traces of L-PAAs clearly visible.

Process_Text.original: The 15 wt% PAA solution was diluted with water to prepare a sizing agent with a concentration of 1 wt%, and the desized CF was then immersed in these PAAs solutions of a same concentration but different molecular weights, followed by removal of excessive sizing agent and drying at 80 °C. The sizing time for DCF fabric was 5 min, while the sizing time for the extracted DCF tows was only 8 s.
Process_Text.simplified: Desized CF was sized in 1 wt% L-PAAs solution, excess removed, then dried at 80 °C; sizing time was 5 min for fabric or 8 s for extracted tows.

Raw_Evidence_Span: A total of four composite laminates with differing molecular weights of PAAs were produced by hot pressing at 350 °C ... and denoted as DCF/PPS, L-CF/PPS, M-CF/PPS, and H-CF/PPS, respectively.
In DCF/PPS composites, the fracture surfaces displayed reduced resin content and substantial gaps between CF and the PPS matrix.

Process_Text.original: CF/PPS composites were fabricated via compression molding, a process that involved the sequential stacking of nine layers of PPS film and eight layers of CF fabric, each measuring 200 × 200 mm. A total of four composite laminates ... were produced by hot pressing at 350 °C (following a preheat of 30 min) under a pressure of 2.5 MPa.
Process_Text.simplified: Stack 9 PPS films and 8 CF fabric layers of 200 × 200 mm, preheat 30 min, hot press at 350 °C and 2.5 MPa.

Structure_Text.original: In DCF/PPS composites, the fracture surfaces displayed reduced resin content and substantial gaps between CF and the PPS matrix, leading to delamination and CF pull-out under stress, which created voids.
Structure_Text.simplified: DCF/PPS has weak CF/PPS interface with gaps, delamination, CF pull-out and voids after flexural fracture.

Structure.Fiber_Architecture: eight layers of 5-harness satin CF fabric with nine PPS film layers

Raw_Evidence_Span: The corresponding CF/PPS composites achieved improvements in interlaminar shear strength (ILSS), flexural strength, and flexural modulus by 66.5 %, 62.1 %, and 22.3 %, respectively.
As shown in Fig. 6(a) and Figs. 7(a,b), the IFSS, ILSS, flexural strength, and modulus of composites utilizing M-PAAs had been enhanced by 68.2%, 62.1%, 66.5%, and 22.3%, respectively.
M-CF/PPS composites exhibited a compact interface with the PPS matrix, reduced CF pull-out, and minimized gaps.
